property_summary: After addReward is called, the migrator state variable is not set in the buggy version while it remains zero in the reference; the test asserts that migrator stays zero after addReward, which passes on the reference (since setMigrator was never called) but fails on the buggy version because the buggy setMigrator still emits the event but doesn't assign the variable, but the property we test is that migrator is never changed from zero, so both versions have migrator = address(0) after addReward—this difference is actually not observable as claimed. Wait, the difference description says after addReward, P.migrator() != M.migrator(). But in the reference, setMigrator is never called, so migrator stays address(0). In the buggy version, setMigrator is also never called, so migrator also stays address(0). The only way to see a difference is to call setMigrator in both. So the concrete witness should call setMigrator with a value, then call addReward, then check migrator. In reference, migrator is set; in bug, it's not set. Let me correct: after calling setMigrator(address(0x123)), then addReward, the reference has migrator = 0x123, bug has migrator = 0. That gives a divergence.
